clue.text: Tragedy is a hit in London, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

blocks.note: taken as written
to lam is to thrash or strike
London is an example of a city, flagged by 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A theatre critic reports that a tragic drama is a big success in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hit' reads like a stage success, but to lam is an old word for thrash; London is just one example of a city, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster or great misfortune, a close synonym of tragedy in everyday speech.

clue.text: Bird lower on farm around river

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a cow lows, so it is a 'lower' on a farm
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bird flies lower over a farm near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like the comparative of low, but it is one who lows, a cow; R goes inside COW to give CROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a large black bird common on farmland, so it is a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Vegetable pleasingly smooth when topped

indicators.note: in a down clue, topping something cuts off its top, its opening letter

blocks.note: sleek means smooth and glossy in an attractive way

explanation.surface: A vegetable looks pleasingly smooth once its top is trimmed off.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEEK loses its first letter S to leave LEEK; 'topped' suits a down entry, where the first letter is at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is a long green-and-white allium eaten as a vegetable, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: More plots being redeveloped outside one big city

indicators.note: redeveloping land rebuilds it in a new layout, so these letters are rearranged
lying outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: More building plots are being redeveloped on the outskirts of a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE PLOTS rearranged gives METROPOLS, which then wraps I just before its final S to make METROPOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a very large and important city, often a capital, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fix furrow up for root vegetable

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, the opposite direction

blocks.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
a rut is a groove or furrow

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a furrow in place to grow root vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN followed by RUT, read upwards, becomes TURNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a round root crop grown and eaten as a vegetable, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Help to contain key corrosive substance

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: aid means help
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Assistance is needed to contain a key corrosive chemical in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important, but it is a musical key, C, which sits inside AID to make ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong acids eat away metal and skin, so a corrosive chemical is a fair general description.

clue.text: Bordeaux securing popular instrument

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
something in is popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A city in France secures a popular musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Bordeaux looks like the city, but it is the wine: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, and it holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind with a cylindrical bore, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Sink vessel carrying small car

indicators.note: to carry something is to bear it within, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a dish is a vessel for food
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A ship goes down while carrying a small car on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' and 'vessel' paint a shipwreck, but the vessel is a DISH, and sink is the verb meaning decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink can mean to decline or dwindle, as prices sink, which is what diminishing does.

clue.text: Obvious vessel to capsize

blocks.note: overt means open and plain to see
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A boat is plainly about to capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat beside 'capsize', but it is an URN, a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to tip over or turn upside down, which is exactly what overturning means.

clue.text: Chopped up most of maple tree

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the last letter is cut
something chopped up is cut into bits and jumbled, so letters are rearranged

blocks.note: maple without its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has chopped up most of a maple tree for firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maple tree' looks like the definition, but the maple is the fodder: MAPL is rearranged into another tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is a tropical tree with a tall trunk and fan-shaped leaves, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Brief moment when a nose condition is limiting

indicators.note: a phrase limiting something sets its bounds, so the letters sit enclosed within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, from the end of 'when' to the middle of 'condition'

explanation.surface: A medical note: a brief moment when a nasal condition is restricting breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of 'when' through 'a nose' into the first four letters of 'condition'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is one billionth of a second, used loosely to mean a very short instant.

clue.text: Notes country in firm control

blocks.note: do and mi are two notes of the sol-fa scale
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country's notes, or memos, reveal its firm grip on power.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes here are the sol-fa syllables DO and MI, not written messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is power exercised over others, which is a strong grip or authority held by one party.

clue.text: Moving about

blocks.note: first meaning: emotionally affecting
second meaning: concerning, on the subject of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving about' reads as walking around, but the words are two separate meanings: one emotional, one a preposition meaning regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective for something that stirs feelings and, formally, as a preposition meaning regarding or concerning.

clue.text: Tree I long in a morning to climb

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so a piece goes within the rest
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
AM is the abbreviation for morning

explanation.surface: Someone longs to climb a tree one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To climb' works only in a down entry, where the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Speaker exposed moral story endlessly

indicators.note: something exposed has had its covering stripped away, so its outer letters go
without ends means both the opening and closing letters are dropped

blocks.note: moral without its first and last letters
story without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A public speaker is exposed for spinning a moral tale that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their outer letters: the inner part of moral, then the inner part of story.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a person who gives public speeches, especially an eloquent one, so it is a specific kind of speaker.

clue.text: A lot sleep with Poles

blocks.note: to doze is to sleep lightly
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Plenty of people have a nap alongside some Polish companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it means the two magnetic poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozens is used informally to mean a large number, many, in the same way as 'a lot'.

clue.text: Decorative pine cover a couple wanted on each end?

blocks.note: surface reading: an attractive skin of wood laid over plainer timber such as pine

blocks.clueFragment: a couple wanted on each end?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the question mark flags a playful extra hint, as though the thin facing layer were needed at both ends of a piece

explanation.surface: A decorative covering for pine furniture, with a pair wanted at either end.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is mostly definition: a thin decorative layer glued over cheaper wood; the questioned tail is a whimsical hint rather than letter-by-letter wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin ornamental sheet of fine wood glued over a plainer base such as pine, so it is a decorative covering.

clue.text: Thought Lab team blue? Just the opposite

blocks.note: Lab is short for Labour; the opposite party is Con, the Conservatives
a side is a team
blue is the Conservative colour; the opposite is Labour's red
an instruction giving no letters: swap the two political words for their rivals

explanation.surface: A scientist muses on a dejected laboratory team, then reverses the thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' swaps each political term: Lab (Labour) becomes Con (Conservative), and blue, the Tory colour, becomes Labour red; team stays as SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought and considered are both past forms of verbs meaning to reflect on or judge something carefully.

clue.text: Power unit leading wagons along train tracks

indicators.note: the leading part of each word is its front, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: An engine supplies power, leading wagons along the railway tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power unit' reads like a locomotive pulling a train, but it is the definition: a unit of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit measuring power, one joule per second, so it is literally a unit of power.

clue.text: Tolerate ecstasy in pub

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A landlord puts up with drug-taking in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy is the drug, abbreviated E, which goes inside BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it, a common synonym of tolerate.

clue.text: Man, say, misled after cover blown

indicators.note: once a cover is blown away nothing wraps it, so the outermost letters are removed

blocks.note: misled without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man was misled after his undercover identity was exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland, so Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: With meal done served up drink

indicators.note: food served up is prepared and plated, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Once dinner is finished, a drink is brought out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' sounds like dinner arriving, but it tells you to rework the letters of meal done.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a sweet soft beverage flavoured with lemon, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Seize returning boat — not the last

indicators.note: leaving out the last means the final letter is dropped
returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat, here without its final letter

explanation.surface: Pirates seize a boat as it returns, though not the last one.
explanation.walkthrough: BARGE loses its final E, then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab is to take hold of something quickly and roughly, a direct synonym of seize.

clue.text: One owed money making changes to record it

indicators.note: changes made to something alter its form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone owed a debt is altering the accounts to record it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record it' looks like bookkeeping, but its eight letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person or company to whom a debt is due, so the phrase describes exactly that role.
